title: Famine MacDonnell Commission
definition: The MacDonnell Commission (1900-1901) was a high-level committee appointed by the British Government under Lord Curzon to investigate the causes of the devastating 1899-1900 famine and to formulate a comprehensive famine relief policy.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the culmination of British famine policy in India, marking a shift from reactive relief to a more structured, preventive administrative framework, frequently appearing in Modern History questions regarding colonial economic exploitation and administrative evolution.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Famine MacDonnell Commission.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Understanding of British Land Revenue Systems (Zamindari, Ryotwari, Mahalwari)
Evolution of British administrative policies in India
